title: add client-side schema prober + streaming slow-path fallback for compatibility layer
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds an opt-in lightweight client schema probe header and server capability response. Introduces a streaming slow-path fallback that preserves tool/function call envelopes for clients that observe degraded streaming behavior.
description:
Background: We see two recurring customer problems: (1) clients that assume a single fixed schema version break when we roll forward small shape changes to structured responses; (2) long-lived streaming connections can silently degrade (slow heartbeats, partial frames) causing downstream tool-calling consumers to mis-parse envelopes. This PR implements a small, opt-in runtime probe plus a stability-driven fallback to make schema evolution safer and streaming more robust for OpenAI-compat clients.

What this change does (high level): 1) Introduces a client probe header (X-Rw-Schema-Probe: {version}) that the compat proxy will accept for a single preflight request and respond with a compact capability object in the X-Rw-Schema-Capabilities response header (capabilities include supported schema versions, streaming-stability flag, tool-envelope-format version, and deprecation warnings). 2) Adds a streaming slow-path detector in the compat proxy runtime: when per-connection heartbeat latency or chunk reassembly errors exceed configured thresholds we transition that stream to a buffered chunk fallback that preserves function/tool-call envelope markers as a JSON array of events. 3) Adds structured-output negotiation so clients can opt into strict typed envelopes (schema=v2-strict) or graceful coercion (schema=v2-coerce). 4) Adds docs and an integration test demonstrating client probe + fallback in a synthetic high-latency scenario.

Checklist:
- [x] Design and spec for probe/capabilities header and server response documented (docs/openapi/schema-probing.md)
- [x] Compat proxy: probe parsing, capability response, and server-side telemetry hooks implemented (src/proxy/schema_prober.go)
- [x] Streaming runtime: heartbeat monitor, slow-path transition, and envelope-preserving buffer implemented (pkg/streaming/slowpath_detector.go)
- [x] Tool/function calling: ensure tool envelope tokens are preserved when transitioning to buffered fallback (pkg/api/compat/tool_envelope.go)
- [x] Backwards compatibility: probe is opt-in; default behavior unchanged if header not present
- [x] Tests: unit + integration (tests/prober_integration_test.go)
- [x] Docs: migration guide and examples (docs/openapi/schema-probing.md)

Commits (summary):
- 9a7b2c1 add schema prober API surface and header parsing
- b3c0e4f implement capability header generation and telemetry counters
- d12f8ee add streaming slow-path detector and buffered fallback implementation
- 5f4a7bc preserve tool envelope markers in buffered output path
- 7c9e0d2 add integration test for probe + slow-path under artificial latency
- 114ef9a docs: add schema-probing migration guide and examples

Files changed (high level):
- src/proxy/schema_prober.go (new): parses X-Rw-Schema-Probe, validates client version, assembles X-Rw-Schema-Capabilities header, emits telemetry.
- pkg/streaming/slowpath_detector.go (new): heartbeat latency tracking, threshold-based transition logic, buffered chunk assembler.
- pkg/api/compat/tool_envelope.go (mod): marker constants and helper to serialize preserved envelopes when switching modes.
- docs/openapi/schema-probing.md (new): spec for probe header, capability header, examples for strict/coerce modes, migration notes.
- tests/prober_integration_test.go (new): simulates 200ms RTT + intermittent frame drops to exercise fallback.
- go.mod / go.sum: dependency bump for a small ringbuffer helper used in the buffered fallback.

Notable implementation details:
- Header shapes: the probe header is intentionally tiny ("X-Rw-Schema-Probe: v2") and the capability header is a base64-encoded compact JSON in "X-Rw-Schema-Capabilities" to avoid interfering with proxies that drop long headers. The server also adds a human-readable JSON to the first event of the fallback buffered stream for diagnostics.
- Streaming fallback behavior: on threshold breach we close the original SSE/time-based stream and open a buffered response that emits a single JSON array composed of the already-emitted events (best-effort) followed by subsequent events as array items. Each event carries an envelope type ("token", "tool-call", "meta"). Tool-call items keep their call_id to allow consumers to reconcile partial calls.
- Observability: added new prometheus counters: compat_probe_received, compat_probe_mismatch, streaming_slowpath_entered, streaming_slowpath_exited. Trace spans added around probe handling and stream-mode-transition.
- Security: probe parsing is read-only; no sensitive request content is echoed in capability headers. We log only capability fingerprints (hashes) in audit logs.

Compatibility notes and migration guidance (brief):
- Default: if clients do not send X-Rw-Schema-Probe nothing changes.
- Opt-in: clients that want smoother upgrades should send the probe header on an initial low-cost request and inspect X-Rw-Schema-Capabilities to learn server-supported schema versions and streaming stability.
- Tool callers: when upgrading to strict schema, clients should validate tool_call envelopes; use "v2-coerce" mode if you need automatic backwards-coercion.

QA and observed behavior:
- Local integration test simulating high latency caused streaming slow-path to be engaged and consumer reassembled the envelope array successfully.
- Load test (small cluster) shows <2% extra tail latency for affected streams; overall throughput unaffected.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag compat.enable_schema_probe (default true for compat tier).
- Stage rollout: nightly for internal tenants, gradual 48-hour ramp on hosted region-by-region with metric alarms on streaming_slowpath_entered > 0.5% of requests.

Follow-ups:
- Add a small client-side helper in SDKs to standardize the probe flow (follow-up PRs to redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript).
- Expose probe capabilities in Console per-token-level breakdown for customers opting in.
